jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.



We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the product roadmap for our core Physical AI capabilities, translating research breakthroughs into deployable, customer-facing products.

 - Sit at the intersection of research, robotics engineering, and field deployment to turn ambiguous technical tradeoffs into clear product decisions.

 - Define what "ready for a customer site" actually means by setting success metrics, reliability thresholds, and scope boundaries for each release.

 - Drive cross-functional alignment across distributed teams in research, engineering, and field operations.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Track record of shipping technical products where the primary challenge was managing complex tradeoffs, not filling out roadmap slides.

 - Deep enough technical understanding to read a policy evaluation, understand a sim-to-real gap, or participate in complex debug sessions and ask the right questions without needing to write the code yourself.

 - Strong bias toward the field over the whiteboard, preferring to evaluate a failed pick on a live customer floor over reading ten synthetic benchmark reports.

 - Exceptional written communication skills to write specs and decision logs that hold up when you're not in the room.

 - Comfort operating with incomplete information in a fast-moving, pre-paradigm field where answers aren't obvious.

 - Bonus: Prior experience in robotics, autonomy, or another domain where "works in the lab" and "works in the world" carry vastly different bars for success.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Deployment
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to work directly with our Head of Deployment to drive execution across our most critical customer deployments. You will operate at the center of complex engineering programs to coordinate AI, robotics, hardware, operations, and customer teams to move our systems from prototype to real-world production.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Partner directly with the Head of Deployment to drive end-to-end execution of customer deployments.

 - Own cross-functional programs spanning robotics software, AI, hardware, infrastructure, operations, and customer success.

 - Coordinate engineering milestones across multiple teams and ensure critical dependencies stay on track.

 - Drive site readiness, including integration planning, testing, validation, site logistics, and launch execution.

 - Engage directly with enterprise customers to translate technical requirements, report progress, and manage timelines.

 - Identify execution risks early and work across engineering teams to resolve technical and operational blockers.

 - Build scalable processes for deployment planning, release management, and customer onboarding.

 - Define how Genesis deploys and scales physical AI and robotics systems across diverse customer environments.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in technical program management, systems engineering, or product operations for complex hardware/software platforms.

 - Technical depth to comfortably navigate technical discussions with software engineers, roboticists, and ML researchers.

 - Track record of leading cross-functional engineering programs from early planning through production rollout.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills to align distributed engineering teams, leadership, and external enterprise stakeholders.

 - Strong systems thinking with a habit of bringing structure to ambiguous operational problems.

 - Willingness to travel to customer sites as needed to support critical deployment milestones.

 - Bonus: Direct experience deploying robotics or autonomous systems into real-world environments.

 - Bonus: Technical background in autonomy, perception, controls, simulation, machine learning, or field engineering.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager (Paris,France)
jobs.description:
SENIOR TECHNICAL PROGRAM MANAGER, PARIS

About Genesis
Genesis is a physical AI research lab and full-stack robotics company building a universal robotics foundation model (one AI "brain" that can power many kinds of robots) and a horizontal robotics platform. We work in San Francisco, Paris and London and combine large-scale AI research, an in-house physics simulation engine, and real robot hardware under one roof.



The role
You'll be the person who turns our most ambitious bets into shipped results. You'll sit between researchers, hardware engineers, software engineers and leadership, across two continents, making sure everyone knows what matters, who owns it and when it lands.



What you'll do

 - Drive cross-functional programs at the frontier of AI and robotics, from foundation model training to hardware–software integration, with pace and accountability

 - Turn ambitious goals into lean, unambiguous roadmaps: clear deliverables, clear owners, clear timelines

 - Dive into robotics hardware, software, simulation, and large-scale AI to understand trade-offs, surface uncertainties, and ask the questions others miss

 - Keep Bay Area and Paris teams tightly aligned, dependencies unblocked, and risks visible early

 - Build lightweight systems (roadmaps, metrics, dashboards) that keep execution focused on what matters

 - Leverage AI to build automated program management workflows, so status updates, risk tracking, and reporting run themselves and the team spends its time on real decisions



What you'll bring

 - 4+ years leading complex technical programs end-to-end in fast-moving environments (startup, research lab, or high-growth tech)

 - Enough technical fluency to hold a real conversation with an ML researcher about a training run and with a hardware engineer about an integration test, so you can challenge an estimate, spot a hidden dependency, or flag a risk before it becomes a delay

 - A track record of learning a new technical domain quickly and becoming useful in it within weeks, not months

 - Crisp, direct communication that aligns researchers, engineers, and leadership

 - Bias for action: many decisions can be reversed and you favor speed over endless analysis

 - Ownership: you own the outcome and drive the process to get tangible results

Bonus

 - Experience in robotics, hardware/software integration, or research workflows

 - Fluency in French
